summary: Verified Daily Purchase Requirement product grouping & banana dozen calculation. Backend /api/retailer-daily-requirement/calculate (GET) returns 74 unique products for 2026-06-10 with variants combined per product_id and correct qty_dozens for Dozen-based products. UI (RetailerOrders > Daily Requirement) correctly renders combined variants column and yellow 'Dozens' input for Banana/Elaichi Banana rows.

issues: Pre-existing React hydration warning: <span> cannot be a child of <option> (caused by x-source-editable instrumentation in retailer dropdown). Cosmetic only, not in current scope.

critical_code_review_comments: RetailerOrders.js is 14389 lines — exceeds 700-line guideline. Should be split into smaller modules (DailyRequirementTable, RejectionLoss, PaymentDetails etc.) for maintainability.

Dozen rounding logic 'Math.ceil(item.qtyDozens)' converts 3.5 dozens (Elaichi Banana) → 4 dozens in the editable input, but the backend still returns the precise 3.5. If the rounded value is later saved, precision is lost. Consider preserving the half-dozen value or making rounding explicit to the user.
calculate endpoint is a GET that performs aggregation across collections without pagination — acceptable now (74 products), but should be monitored as catalog grows.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (verified Banana, Elaichi Banana, Onion, Tomato Hybrid, Jamun, Bottle Gourd)

test_credentials: admin@freshflow.com / admin123 (login API requires 'identifier' field, not 'email')
seed_data_creation: None - used existing indents for target_date=2026-06-10
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend uses GET /api/retailer-daily-requirement/calculate?target_date=YYYY-MM-DD (NOT POST). Login payload must use 'identifier' key. For UI test, RetailerOrders page has 3 date inputs; the Daily Requirement section uses the LAST date input (index 2). Click 'Daily Requirement' tab button first.
